name: spencer-1986
url: https://github.com/garyhouston/regexp.old (git clone, single commit c7db272ecea9e0a6b2139585cd38886c500efe35 'import' 2014-12-26; this is Henry Spencer's 1986 regexp(3) as revised 1993/1995 for 'Software Solutions in C' - README and COPYRIGHT read from src/, GitHub page fetched)
files_measured: src/regexp.c (1093 lines; regcomp+regexec = the whole engine) measured with -Isrc. Also measured but NOT counted: src/regsub.c (regsub() substitution helper, 221 B) and src/regerror.c (default error handler = fprintf+exit, 47 B; replaced by a stub in any embedding). Not measured: try.c, timer.c (test/timing programs).
per_function_top: Cortex-M4 -Os (regexp.c, all 17 sections sum to 2751): regbranch 932 (regpiece and regatom inlined into it); regmatch 500 (regrepeat inlined); regcomp 248; reg 240; .rodata.regbranch.str1.1 168; regexec 152; .rodata.regmatch.str1.1 75; .rodata.reg.str1.1 69; then rodata.regcomp 53, regtry 52, reginsert 52, regtail 48, rodata.regexec 42, regnode 34, regoptail 30, regnext 30, regc 26. The 407 B of .rodata are 21 error-message strings passed to regerror() ('*+ operand could be empty', 'unmatched []', ...) plus the 12-byte META table '^$.[()|?+*\\'; engine code proper is ~2344 B.
excluded_functions: Nothing excluded from regexp.c: regdump()/regprop() exist only under #ifdef DEBUG and are not compiled. Excluded files: regsub.c (substitution API, not matching), regerror.c (default handler that prints and exit()s), try.c/timer.c (tests). regexp.c+regsub.c+regerror.c would be 2751+221+47 = 3019 B.
libc_deps: arm-none-eabi-nm -u regexp_m4.o: malloc (regcomp allocates the compiled program), memmove (reginsert), memset (regtry clearing startp/endp, compiler-generated), strchr (ANYOF/ANYBUT membership and regstart scan), strcspn (regatom literal run, ANYBUT repeat), strlen, strncmp (EXACTLY), strspn (ANYOF repeat), strstr (regmust prefilter), regerror (user-supplied callback). No memcmp, no setjmp, no ctype, no stdio at link time (stdio.h included but unused). regsub.c adds _ctype_ (isdigit) + strncpy; regerror.c adds fprintf, exit, _impure_ptr.
ram_model: malloc: YES, one allocation per regcomp() of sizeof(regexp)+program (header 96 B on ARM: startp[10]+endp[10] pointers + regstart/reganch/regmust/regmlen; program = 3 B per node + operand bytes, character classes stored as an expanded byte list: 'a'=12 B, 'abc'=14, '(a|b)+c'=46, '[a-z]'=37, '[^a-zA-Z0-9_]'=74, '^([a-z]+)@([a-z]+)\\.com$'=114, measured via malloc hook). Compile is two-pass (size pass then emit pass) so exactly one malloc, freed by the caller; no allocation during regexec. Program limited to <0x7fff bytes (2-byte next pointers). Stack (-fstack-usage, M4): regmatch 32 B/frame and it recurses on itself at every OPEN, CLOSE, BRANCH-with-alternatives and STAR/PLUS backtrack point along the current path; a looped group like (ab)* costs ~3-4 frames (~100-130 B) per iteration, so depth grows with text length for quantified groups; no depth guard. Compile recursion reg(40 B)+regbranch(56 B) = 96 B per parenthesis nesting level; regcomp frame 48 B (struct comp), regexec 32 B. No static/global state (reentrant); captures live in the regexp struct. Text and pattern must be NUL-terminated C strings (no length parameter), so NUL cannot appear in either.
difftest:
python3 difftest.py ./engine_cli corpus_seed1.jsonl -> cases=2088 checked=2081 pass=1029 fail=1052 timeouts=1 group_spans_checked=78 (49.4% pass). Driver adaptation: none needed for search/captures (regexec searches anywhere and fills startp/endp[1..9]); '-i' is accepted and IGNORED because the engine has no case-insensitive mode (counted as missing feature); regerror() replaced by a non-exiting stub that prints the message to stderr (default regerror.c calls exit). Classification of the 1052 (classify.py, primary reason in priority order): MISSING FEATURES 1006 = (?:...) non-capturing group 408 (regcomp error '?+* follows nothing'); lazy quantifiers *? +? ?? {n,m}? 353 (error 'nested *?+', or wrong span when after '}'); -i case-insensitive flag 111; \d \w \s \D \W \S 78 (\d = literal 'd'); {n,m} counted repetition 56 (treated as literal text). c' -> match); no backslash escapes inside [] 1 ('[\]]' on 'a]b' -> nomatch). TIMEOUT 1 = '^(a+)+$' on 27 a's + 'b' (exponential backtracking, no step limit). BUGS: 0 found - a bug-check run on the 140-case corpus subset that uses only Spencer-supported syntax (no -i, (?, lazy, {n,m}, \letter, non-ASCII,

Secondary 'any-reason' counts (a case can carry several): UTF-8 text/pattern 886, \d\w\s 749, lazy 702, {n,m} 564, (?: 455, -i 111, empty-operand 45,   4, C escapes 3. The 7 expected-error cases were skipped by the harness.
caveats: (1) 2751 B is regexp.c alone; ~407 B of that is diagnostic strings (21 regerror messages + META table), so the matching/compiling code proper is ~2.35 KB; libc pulls (strchr/strcspn/strspn/strstr/strncmp/strlen/memmove/memset + malloc) are extra at link time. (2) The engine is a byte matcher from 1986: no {n,m}, no lazy, no (?:, no \d\w\s, no \b, no case folding, no UTF-8 - the corpus exercises all of these heavily (see any-reason counts), which is why it passes only 49%; on the syntax it does implement it is correct (134/140) with Perl-compatible leftmost-first alternation and last-iteration captures. (3) Requires malloc (one block per compiled pattern) and uses unbounded recursion in regmatch (32 B/frame on M4, depth ~ number of choice points on the current path, grows with text length for quantified groups) - no depth or step guard, so '^(a+)+$' hangs (classic exponential case). (4) Rejects any * or + whose operand can match empty ((a*)*, (a|)+ etc.) - man page calls this 'an artifact of the simplistic implementation'. (5) '$' matches only at the NUL terminator and '.' matches newline; '^' only at offset 0 - semantics differ from Python/Perl on texts containing \n. (6) API is NUL-terminated strings only (regexec(regexp*, const char*)); no length argument, no NUL in text. (7) Character classes are stored as an expanded byte list (3 B + one byte per member), so [^a-z] costs ~30 B of program per class; a 2-byte next-pointer format caps the program at 32 KB. (8) K&R-style function definitions: compiles with -w today but clang warns 'not supported in C23'; -std=gnu99 was used as per protocol. (9) License: custom permissive notice (COPYRIGHT file: use/redistribute freely, no misrepresentation, keep notice). (10) The survey agent's earlier measurement in engines/spencer86/BUILD.txt (same repo, different clone path) gave identical numbers (2751/2759/5051), confirming reproducibility. (11) 9-group limit (NSUBEXP=10) is a compile-time constant; raising it enlarges the OPEN/CLOSE switch and the regexp header.
